sources.entry: OpenReader - EPUB, PDF, DOCX, MD, and TXT file text to speech document reader. Read documents in realtime with high-quality TTS; or extract audiobooks. (Source Code) MIT Docker

summary.one_liner: OpenReader is a self-hostable, Next.js-based text-to-speech document reader that plays EPUB, PDF, TXT, MD, and DOCX files with synchronized read-along highlighting and audiobook export.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes a web app that reads documents aloud with multilingual, synchronized read-along playback for EPUB, PDF, TXT, MD, and DOCX files. It offers multiple TTS backends: local Kokoro with no API key, self-hosted OpenAI-compatible servers (Kokoro-FastAPI, KittenTTS-FastAPI, Orpheus-FastAPI, Supertonic), and cloud APIs (OpenAI, Replicate, Google AI Studio, Fish Audio, OpenRouter). PDF parsing is layout-aware using PP-DocLayoutV3 (ONNX), and word-by-word highlighting is available. Users can export audiobooks as M4B or MP3, and can record or import a voice sample for narration with supported providers. Storage can be embedded SeaweedFS or S3-compatible, with SQLite or Postgres for the database. A separate desktop app for macOS, Windows, and Linux is also offered, and the project ships Docker images for amd64 and arm64.
use_cases: listen to PDFs or ebooks read aloud
self-host a text-to-speech reader for a team or family
read EPUB files with synchronized word highlighting
narrate documents with a cloned personal voice
run offline TTS reading with local Kokoro voices
how_to_run: Download the desktop app from the project's releases page (macOS, Windows, Linux)
Run with Docker Compose (see the Docker Compose docs linked in the README)
Deploy on Vercel (see Vercel Deployment docs)
notable: Progressive background generation: playback starts after the first segment while the worker generates ahead, with cached audio reused across seeks and exports
Word-by-word highlighting using Kokoro phoneme durations or ONNX Whisper alignment
Multi-provider TTS covering local Kokoro, self-hosted OpenAI-compatible servers, and several cloud APIs
Audiobook export to M4B or MP3 assembled by the compute worker
caveats: Full self-hosted setup involves a compute worker with NATS JetStream and optional object storage, which adds infrastructure
Available languages and voices depend on the configured TTS provider
Cloud TTS providers and voice cloning features require third-party API access
